key_insight: t-GQCE combines classical lattice propagation with quantum embedding dynamics to capture correlated-electron evolution, approaching nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory results as ghost orbitals are added.
engineering_relevance: The framework assigns finite interacting problems to quantum processors while keeping noninteracting lattice dynamics classical, exchanging only Hamiltonian parameters and single-particle density matrices.
method: Map lattice dynamics to coupled quasiparticle and interacting embedding models using the time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller approximation.
Propagate the lattice classically and embedding states with a quantum dynamics solver.
Use adaptive circuits, circuit compression, rotated-basis measurements, post-selection, and noise mitigation.
evidence_signal: Hubbard-model quench tests achieved embedding-state infidelities below 5×10⁻⁴ in 8–16-qubit statevector simulations; reduced-noise tests reached 0.01 accuracy for density matrices and double occupancy with 10⁵ shots per time step.
watch_item: The reported noisy-simulation accuracy required mitigation and error rates one third of a hardware-benchmarked model; the IBM hardware demonstration used only one embedding qubit plus an ancilla.
paper_title: Gutzwiller Quantum-Classical Embedding for Dynamics Simulations of Correlated Electron Systems
